-## reference · generative engine optimization
-* Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring web content so that AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Claude cite it as a source when generating answers.
-* The original Princeton + Georgia Tech + IIT Delhi study proved GEO methods can lift content visibility in AI answers by up to 40% — with “Statistics Addition,” “Cite Sources,” and “Quotation Addition” driving the biggest gains.
-* Organic CTR has collapsed 61% on Google queries where an AI Overview appears.
-* AI traffic is the highest-ROI channel on the web: ChatGPT converts at 14.2–15.9%, Perplexity at 10.5%, Claude at up to 16.8% — vs. Google organic’s 1.76%.
-* The overlap between Google’s top-10 organic results and AI citations has crashed from ~75% in mid-2025 to 17–38% in early 2026.
-* 44.2% of all LLM citations come from the first 30% of a page.
-* Only 14% of marketers track AI search performance today.
-* Traditional SEO is not dead, but it has been absorbed into a larger discipline called Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), where success is measured by citations inside AI-generated answers.
-* The four-stage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline used by modern AI search products includes Query Fan-Out, Information Retrieval, Synthesis, and Citation Attribution.
-* AI engines do not cite pages — they cite passages, so the practical job of GEO is to make every paragraph independently extractable.
-* The 9 GEO ranking factors that actually move citations in 2026 include:
-  1. Fact Density (Statistics per 100 words): at least 1 verifiable statistic, named entity, or specific date every 100 words for informational content.
-  2. Direct-Answer Lead in the First 30% of the Page.
-  3. Structured Extractability: pages with FAQ schema and inline citations are weighted approximately 40% higher in ChatGPT source selection.
-  4. Entity Authority over Backlinks.
-  5. Statistics Addition: inject specific numbers (percentages, counts, dollar amounts, dates).
-  6. Quotation Addition: include direct, attributable quotes from credible third parties.
-  7. Cite Sources: add inline references to your own claims.
-  8. Time-to-impact: 4–8 weeks for retrieval-based engines like ChatGPT Search and Perplexity.
-  9. Citation Attribution: sources that contributed specific facts to the draft get an inline citation.

+## reference · generative engine optimization 2026 tactics statistics quotations
+
+- **GEO definition**: structure content so LLM‑powered engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot) retrieve, trust, and cite it in generated answers.  
+- **Visibility lift**: targeted GEO methods can raise AI answer visibility by **up to 40 %** (Princeton/Georgia Tech/KDD 2024).  
+- **Key citation drivers** (KDD 2024):  
+  - **Statistics Addition** – insert specific numbers (percentages, counts, dollar amounts, dates).  
+  - **Quotation Addition** – embed direct, attributable quotes from credible third parties.  
+  - **Cite Sources** – add inline references to your own claims; 5th‑ranked pages saw a **+115.1 %** relative visibility lift.  
+- **Fact density target**: ≥ 1 verifiable statistic, named entity, or specific date per 100 words for informational content.  
+- **Lead‑answer rule**: place the core answer in the first 30 % of the page; 44.2 % of LLM citations originate there (Zyppy 2025).  
+- **Structured extractability**:  
+  - FAQ schema + inline citations ≈ 40 % higher ChatGPT source weight.  
+  - ≥ 3 schema types → 13 % higher LLM citation probability (Authoritas 2025).  
+- **Entity authority > backlinks**: LLMs prioritize authoritative entities over backlink signals.  
+- **Time to impact**: 4–8 weeks for retrieval‑based engines (ChatGPT Search, Perplexity); months for engines that rely on training‑data inclusion.  
+- **Organic CTR drop**: 61 % decline when an AI Overview appears (Seer 2025).  
+- **AI traffic share**: ChatGPT accounts for ~17 % of global digital queries (QuickSEO 2026).  
+- **AI referral ROI**: ChatGPT conversion 14.2–15.9 %, Perplexity 10.5 %, Claude up to 16.8 % vs. Google organic 1.76 % (Seer 2025; First Page Sage 2026).  
+- **Overlap decline**: Google top‑10 vs. AI citations fell from ~75 % (mid‑2025) to 17–38 % (early 2026) (Demand Local 2026; BrightEdge 2026).  
+- **AI citation concentration**: 44.2 % of all LLM citations come from the first 30 % of a page (Zyppy 2025).  
+- **Tracking gap**: only 14 % of marketers track AI search performance (Conductor 2026).  
+
